## The request this plan answers

> Review the repo and generate a step-by-step iterative work /plan with high /effort that encompasses exploratory analysis, spatial analysis, and statistical analysis. I want you to evaluate the data structure and distribution, identifying any caveats or limitations. Then recommend the most appropriate treatments or transformations of the vessel presence and apparent fishing effort data. I am most interested in analyzing cell x stage x gear and cell x month x gear relationships for the primary sets. For the spatial analysis, begin with Global Moran's I and Getis-Ord General G, then compare the efficacy of a Local Moran's I vs. Getis-Ord Gi* analysis. Following these tests, I want to assess the value of calculating and visualizing an autocorrelated kernel density estimate. I will gather turbine and cable location data with installation dates from Orsted, so we can also execute the BAG spatial-temporal models. Provide me with a comparison of approaches for a Tweedie GLMM, Hurdle model, or an Bayesian INLA-SPDE, including what conditions each of these approaches would require. I want the subsequent workflow to be written in R and grounded in FAIR data principles. Name the plan as gfw_analysis_plan.qmd in \planning. Include this prompt at the top of the document. If you have any questions, interview me.
:::

## Summary

The R workflow (`r/01`–`r/04`) ends with zero-filled cell tables for the
**Primary** and **Strict** sets. This plan covers everything after that, as
numbered qmds `r/05`–`r/14`. Each phase ends at a decision gate, and the
answer at each gate can change the next phase.

Six findings from profiling the current outputs (2026-10-06 pull, measured
2026-10-18) shape the design. Each is covered in @sec-structure and
@sec-caveats.

1. **The two datasets have different statistical shapes.** Vessel presence (VP)
   hours are effectively integer counts of *vessel × cell × day occupancy*:
   96.2% of Primary VP records are exactly 1 h. Apparent fishing effort (AFE)
   is continuous and non-negative with exact zeros. The monthly mean–variance
   power slope is about 1.2 for VP and about 1.7 for AFE. So VP calls for a
   **negative-binomial count model** and AFE for a **Tweedie or delta
   (hurdle) model**. One family for both would be wrong for one of them.
2. **Cell × month AFE is extremely sparse, and coarser time steps reduce the
   sparsity but do not remove it.** Monthly AFE is 97.7% zeros for mobile
   gear, 99.2% for fixed and 99.7% for pole-and-line. Of 3,376 cells, 1,941
   never have fixed-gear AFE and 2,775 never have pole-and-line AFE. Even
   within each gear's Stage 1 domain, mobile AFE is still 83.5% zeros at a
   two-season step and 70.4% at a yearly one. The zeros come from the few
   vessels logging fishing, not from the time step. So the plan:
   - uses **one set of time steps for every gear and dataset in the
     descriptive statistics and maps**: stage, stage × season (Apr–Sep /
     Oct–Mar) and season-year. Spatial statistics change with temporal
     aggregation, so steps that differed by gear would confound gear with
     step;
   - lets the **models** differ only where the data require it: a shared
     stage × season model for every modelled gear, and a timing model that is
     monthly for VP and mobile AFE and season-year for fixed AFE
     (@sec-time-steps).
3. **The stage means mix in different seasons, and dividing by stage length
   does not fix it.** Stage 2 (Oct 2020 – Mar 2023) holds three of each winter
   month but only two of each summer month. 33% of its months fall in May–Sep,
   which carries 78% of fixed-gear AFE, against 44% in Stage 1 and 46% in
   Stage 3. A per-month rate treats every month as having the same expected
   effort, so it inherits each stage's calendar mix. The raw rate understates
   Stage 2 fixed-gear AFE by 11.9% against a season-standardised rate, while
   mobile gear is within 3%. The plan compares stages within the same season
   (stage × season), uses season-standardised rates for level comparisons, and
   handles season inside the models with a season term rather than by adjusting
   the data (caveat 8).
4. **A few vessels drive the effort signal.** The top 5 MMSIs carry 50% of
   Primary fixed-gear AFE, and one vessel carries 40% of pole-and-line AFE.
   PROVIDER (367717050) had June–September 2020 activity (1,452 AFE h) that
   looked like its charter work: 66% of hours inside the leases, against 23.3%
   for the rest of the Stage 1 fleet. Its charter window now starts on
   **2020-06-18**, the first day of that in-lease activity. That cuts Stage 1
   mobile AFE by 16% (caveat 11 in @sec-caveats).
5. **Global autocorrelation is strong in every surface.** Moran's I runs from
   0.20 to 0.77 and every z exceeds 23. The global tests will therefore confirm
   clustering rather than discover it. Their value is in comparing effect sizes
   across gear and stage, and in setting the spatial scale for the later
   models.
6. **The BAG gradient is short and has no far-field control.** Every cell lies
   within about 15 km of a lease. 893 cells (26%) are inside one, and only 130
   are more than 10 km away. With the within-AOI design chosen in the
   interview, BAG supports inference about **redistribution relative to the
   outer ring**, not about net change in regional effort.

## Data structure and distribution {#sec-structure}

All figures are for the **Primary set** unless labelled otherwise. They were
measured on 2026-10-18 from the 2026-10-06 pull, after PROVIDER's window
moved to 2020-06-18 and 03 and 04 were re-run. `06_explore.qmd` recomputes
every one of them at render time, so these typed values are a record of what
justified the design, not values to quote.

### Grid and support

- **3,376 cells**: 3,118 `inside`, 206 `edge`, 52 `outside`.
- `area_km2` ranges from 0.929 to 0.937. The 0.9% range means the area offset
  barely changes the results, but keep it so results are in density units
  (h km⁻² month⁻¹) and stay comparable with other grids.
- Queen contiguity, rebuilt from the `ix`/`iy` lattice, gives a mean of 7.80
  neighbours, one connected component and no islands. 02's `poly2nb()` on the
  corner-built grid should give the same weights. Phase 0 asserts that they
  match.

### Composition of the Primary set

| | VP | AFE |
|---|---:|---:|
| Records | 93,295 | 20,241 |
| MMSIs | 1,381 | 414 |
| MOBILE MMSIs / hours | 771 / 66,599 | 277 / 23,374 |
| FIXED MMSIs / hours | 138 / 21,842 | 61 / 5,215 |
| POLE_AND_LINE MMSIs / hours | 473 / 9,976 | 76 / 2,023 |
| UNRESOLVED hours | **0** | **0** |

Every Primary record has a resolved gear class, so the `UNRESOLVED` rows in the
Primary gear tables are structural zeros. Drop them in Phase 0. In Strict,
`UNRESOLVED` carries 58,078 AFE hours in Stage 3, so a gear-specific Strict
analysis is not interpretable. Strict is used only for all-gear comparisons.

### Record-level distributions

- **VP hours per record** are integers from 1 to 15. 96.2% are exactly 1 h,
  2.9% are 2 h and 0.3% are more than 3 h. A cell-month VP total is therefore
  close to a count of **vessel-days with at least one AIS position in the
  cell**. It measures occupancy and is dominated by transits.
- **AFE hours per record**: median 1.00, 90th percentile 2.86, 99th percentile
  11.1, maximum 24.3. 64 records are exactly 0 h and 1,708 are below 0.32 h.
  The archived Python pipeline dropped records at or below 0.32 h; the R
  pipeline keeps them. Keep them, and add a sensitivity run that drops them.

### Cell × stage × gear

| Gear | VP % zero (S1/S2/S3) | VP var/mean | AFE % zero (S1/S2/S3) | AFE var/mean |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| MOBILE | 8.9 / 22.9 / 8.4 | 10.7–15.5 | 52.2 / 72.4 / 39.6 | 11–22 |
| FIXED | 36.8 / 33.9 / 15.0 | 2.7–5.8 | 86.2 / 87.8 / 71.9 | 7.6–10.6 |
| POLE_AND_LINE | 61.2 / 65.6 / 40.8 | 6.8–26 | 95.2 / 93.8 / 89.0 | 10–57 |

- Every cell is overdispersed (variance/mean well above 1), so Poisson does not
  fit.
- Stage 2 has more zeros than both neighbours for VP mobile and AFE mobile and
  fixed. The gap is widest for mobile AFE: 72.4% zero in Stage 2, against
  52.2% in Stage 1 and 39.6% in Stage 3, with all of PROVIDER's charter hours
  excluded. **Zero shares are not comparable across stages of different
  length.** A cell has 30 months to record any effort in Stage 2, against 57
  and 41, so a shorter stage has more zeros even at identical monthly effort.
  Season composition adds little for mobile gear: its rate bias is under 3%
  (caveat 8). Split by season, the Stage 2 mobile AFE gap sits in Apr–Sep
  (83.6% zero, against 58.0% in Stage 1 and 59.1% in Stage 3), while Oct–Mar
  is level across stages (83.5 / 83.0 / 61.6). Stage × season comparisons
  (@sec-time-steps) are the fair view.
- A typical occupied cell has 1–4 MMSIs. For fixed and pole-and-line gear, a
  third to a half of occupied cells hold one vessel only.

### Cell × month × gear

| Gear | VP % zero | AFE % zero | VP cells never active | AFE cells never active | VP median active months (of 128) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MOBILE | 89.3 | 97.7 | 47 | 657 | 8 |
| FIXED | 95.6 | 99.2 | 128 | 1,941 | 4.5 |
| POLE_AND_LINE | 98.2 | 99.7 | 735 | 2,775 | 2 |

**Mean–variance power** (slope of log variance on log mean across cells, monthly):

| | MOBILE | FIXED | POLE_AND_LINE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| VP | 1.18 | 1.12 | 1.24 |
| AFE | 1.67 | 1.67 | 1.71 |

This is a first estimate of the Tweedie power *p*. For VP, *p* ≈ 1.2 is close
to the Poisson boundary, which supports a count family. For AFE, *p* ≈ 1.7
sits well inside the compound Poisson–gamma range (1 < *p* < 2).

**Seasonality.** Share of hours by month-of-year:

- Fixed-gear AFE: 78% falls in May–Sep, 80.5% in Apr–Sep, and 4.3% in Dec–Feb.
- Mobile AFE: 57% falls in Apr–Sep. Its effort is spread through the year
  (Dec–Feb 18%, Sep–Nov 31%).
- Pole-and-line AFE: 53% falls in Apr–Sep.
- Mobile VP: 40% falls in Jun–Aug.
- Pole-and-line VP: 47% falls in Jul–Aug.

Every monthly model needs a cyclic month-of-year term, and every stage-level
model a season term.

**Trend in AIS coverage.** Distinct Primary MMSIs per year rose from 354
(2016) to 603 (2025) for VP, and from 63 to 129 for AFE. Fixed-gear VP rose
from 25 to 280 occupied cells per month. Part of that rise is AIS uptake, not
effort (@sec-cav-ais).

### Global spatial autocorrelation (preview)

Queen weights, row-standardised, on √(hours ÷ months ÷ km²). Analytic
randomisation z in brackets.

| Moran's I | S1 | S2 | S3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| VP MOBILE | 0.77 (88) | 0.70 (80) | 0.73 (84) |
| VP FIXED | 0.43 (49) | 0.25 (29) | 0.50 (57) |
| VP POLE_AND_LINE | 0.29 (33) | 0.27 (31) | 0.37 (43) |
| AFE MOBILE | 0.42 (48) | 0.40 (46) | 0.56 (64) |
| AFE FIXED | 0.33 (37) | 0.24 (28) | 0.47 (54) |
| AFE POLE_AND_LINE | 0.20 (24) | 0.23 (27) | 0.24 (27) |

General G z-scores follow Moran's I closely (24–81). Two points stand out:
clustering of fixed gear rises sharply into Stage 3 in both datasets, and the
Stage 2 dip shows again.

## Caveats and limitations {#sec-caveats}

Each caveat comes with the treatment this plan applies to it. Report them in
the methods with numbers recomputed at render time, not typed.

### Measurement

1. **VP hours count occupancy, not duration.** VP is the number of hours with
   at least one position, so a vessel crossing a cell scores 1 h whether it
   stays 5 minutes or 59. *Treatment:* model VP as a count and describe it as
   "vessel-day occupancy" in the text. Do not add VP and AFE hours together.
2. **AFE is a model output, not observed fishing.** GFW's fishing classifier is
   most accurate for trawlers, longliners and purse seiners. It is less
   validated for pots, traps and gillnets, whose AIS tracks look like slow
   transits. *Treatment:* state it. Treat fixed-gear AFE as the least reliable
   surface, and have VP replicate every fixed-gear finding.
3. **AFE is near zero, by construction, for the 142 hulls Primary adds.** GFW
   computes effort only for vessels it types as fishing. *Treatment:* the
   sensitivity run uses the imputation already in `04` (@sec-sensitivity).
4. **Sub-threshold AFE.** 1,708 Primary AFE records are below 0.32 h, 64 of
   them exactly 0. *Treatment:* keep them, and add a sensitivity run that drops them.

### Coverage and representativeness {#sec-cav-ais}

5. **AIS carriage is uneven by gear and changes over time.** The 2016 USCG rule
   requires AIS on commercial fishing vessels of 65 ft and over. Most SNE
   pot and gillnet boats are smaller and carry AIS voluntarily, so fixed gear
   and pole-and-line are **undercounted, and the undercount shrinks over
   time**. The 10× rise in occupied fixed-gear VP cells from 2016 to 2025
   is partly uptake.
   *Treatment:*
   - In the BAG design, an AOI-wide uptake trend cancels out of the gradient
     contrast, but only if uptake is **spatially uniform** across the distance
     bands. Check that assumption (Phase 1, step 7).
   - Add a fleet-size covariate (active MMSIs per gear per month, AOI-wide) as
     a sensitivity term.
   - Report `rate_fleet` (hours per vessel-month) next to `rate` in every
     stage-level table. If `rate` rises while `rate_fleet` stays flat, the
     rise is fleet coverage, not more fishing per vessel. The fleet count can
     itself respond to the projects: vessels that leave the AOI because of
     them lower the denominator. A regional MMSI count from outside the AOI
     avoids that and is preferred if one is available. New adopters are
     mostly small fixed-gear boats with few hours, so `rate_fleet` falls from
     that change in fleet mix alone. Never divide by per-cell n_MMSI. That
     hides avoidance (fewer vessels in a cell is the signal) and leaves every
     empty cell at 0/0.
   - Never interpret a rise in AOI-total effort as more fishing.
6. **No external control.** With the within-AOI design (interview decision), an
   AOI-wide change cannot be separated from regional trends, the 2020 COVID
   market disruption or AIS uptake. *Treatment:* claims are limited to spatial
   redistribution relative to the 8–15 km ring (@sec-bag-limits).
7. **Possible AIS switch-off.** Vessels can stop transmitting near construction
   for security or competitive reasons. That would look like avoidance.
   *Treatment:* state it as an alternative explanation. If an MMSI
   disappears inside the leases during construction but stays active
   elsewhere, its gaps can be checked in the record-level data.

### Design

8. **Season composition differs between stages**. Stage 2 is
   33% May–Sep months; Stages 1 and 3 are 44% and 46%. Dividing by stage
   length (caveat 9) does not correct this: a per-month rate is an average of
   monthly rates weighted by the stage's calendar mix, much as a crude death
   rate depends on a population's age structure. Bias of the raw AOI stage
   rate against the season-standardised rate (the mean of the 12
   month-of-year means within the stage):

   | Gear (AFE) | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|
   | FIXED | +4.7% | **−11.9%** | +3.7% |
   | MOBILE | +1.6% | −2.6% | −2.6% |
   | POLE_AND_LINE | −3.5% | 0.0% | +4.1% |

   For fixed gear the calendar alone could produce a "Stage 2 dip" of up to
   about 16% against its neighbours. The correction matters mainly for fixed
   gear, the most seasonal.

   Standardisation adds almost no noise. Every calendar month appears 2–5
   times in every stage, so it only re-weights months gently (in Stage 2, ×1.25
   for Apr–Sep months and ×0.83 for Oct–Mar). The effective sample size falls
   by at most 4%: 28.8 of 30 months in Stage 2 and 40.2 of 41 in Stage 3. At
   cell level, standardised and raw Stage 2 surfaces correlate at r ≥ 0.99.
   *Treatment:*
   - **Level comparisons** (stage rate tables, density-difference maps
     between stages, the descriptive BAG): report season-standardised rates
     next to the raw ones.
   - **Spatial statistics:** raw rates. Moran's I, General G, LISA and Gi\*
     are unchanged when a surface is multiplied by a constant, and season
     bias mostly moves a whole stage up or down, so standardising gains
     little.
   - **Stage × season** (@sec-time-steps) compares like with like and removes
     most of the bias without standardising: the bias left within a stage ×
     season stratum is at most 4.6%.
   - **Models:** never standardise the response. Rescaled hours are no longer
     counts (NB2 for VP) and distort the Tweedie mean–variance relationship.
     The models carry a season term (stage × season tables) or a cyclic month
     term (monthly tables), estimated from all the data.
9. **Stage lengths differ** (57 / 30 / 41 months). *Treatment:* use rates (hours
   ÷ months) in descriptives and an offset of `log(months × area_km2)` in the
   models. Rates fix the length difference only; the calendar mix is caveat 8.
   **Zero shares** are not length-corrected by any rate: a shorter stage has
   more zero cells at the same monthly effort. Compare zero shares only within
   strata of similar length, or through the models, whose offset handles it.
10. **One window holds very different disturbances.** Stage 3 combines seabed
    preparation, construction and operation at three projects on different
    schedules. The interview kept the three stages. *Treatment:* the monthly
    BAG uses the Ørsted dates to give each cell its own exposure timing.
11. **PROVIDER's Stage 1 activity in 2020 looked like charter work.** With
    its window starting on 2020-10-01, it kept 1,452 AFE h and 1,651 VP h
    before that date, almost all from June to September 2020 (it has 1 AFE h
    in total before 2020).
    - Those months put 66% of its AFE hours inside the leases (36% in June
      rising to 80% in September) at 17 h per active day.
    - Its confirmed charter period is 55–64% in the leases at 16–19 h per day.
    - The rest of the Stage 1 fleet is 23.3% (AFE) and 16.1% (VP) inside the
      leases, so PROVIDER's pre-window share was about three times the
      fleet's. (Measured with PROVIDER's own pre-window hours in the fleet,
      the shares were 28.9% / 18.3%.)

    A screen of every charter hull's last 12 months before its window
    finds no other case: the next highest is Ashley Ann (338328681) at 20%
    (AFE). PROVIDER made up 1,452 of the 2,878 h (50%) of Primary mobile AFE
    in June–September 2020.

    **Decision (2026-10-18, D-011):** `valid_from` moved from 2020-10-01 to
    **2020-06-18** in `references/vessel_decisions.csv`.

    *Reasoning:*
    - Orsted and Sea Services North America began a pilot contract for 
      chartered safety vessels in 2020.
    - 2020-06-18 is the first day with in-lease hours in both VP and AFE.
      From then the pattern runs unbroken, at 16–20 h per day, into the
      confirmed window.
    - Before 2020 the hull has no fishing baseline to depart from: 1 AFE h
      (2018) and scattered 1–4 h VP days in the summers of 2017–2019.
    - The in-lease share and daily intensity match its confirmed charter
      period, not the fleet's.
    - It is the only charter hull with this pattern.

    One day before the window, 2020-06-09 (4 AFE h, outside the leases),
    stays as fishing, as do all earlier records. The window starts before
    Stage 2 (2020-10-01), so this row is a dated exclusion inside Stage 1. It
    does not follow the `stages_2_3` convention of the removal list.

    *Effect, measured after the re-run of 03 and 04 (2026-10-18):*

    | Primary, mobile gear | Before | After |
    |---|---:|---:|
    | Stage 1 AFE hours | 9,213 | 7,765 (−16%) |
    | Stage 1 AFE zero cells | 43.2% | 52.2% |
    | Stage 1 VP hours | 27,826 | 26,207 (−6%) |
    | Jun–Sep 2020 AFE hours | 2,878 | 1,430 |
    | Stage 1 AFE Moran's I | 0.44 | 0.42 |

    PROVIDER's only Primary AFE record is now 2020-06-09.

    *Treatment:*
    - Make the pre-window screen a standing check in `06` (Phase 1, step 5),
      so every charter window is tested against the activity just before it.
    - Phase 7 keeps the "exclude 2020" run, for COVID and the stage boundary.

### Statistical

12. **Effort is concentrated in few vessels.** For fixed AFE the top 5 vessels
    carry 50% and the top 10 carry 72%. For pole-and-line AFE one vessel
    carries 40%. A cell's value often comes from a single hull. *Treatment:*
    - Run a leave-one-vessel-out jackknife over the top 10 MMSIs per gear on
      every headline result.
    - As an optional extension, fit a vessel-level model with an MMSI random
      effect (@sec-models-vessel).
    - Report n_MMSI next to every map.
13. **Exact zeros: structural or sampling?** A zero in a cell that a gear never
    uses (wrong depth or substrate, a closure) is structural. A zero in a
    fished cell in a quiet month is sampling. *Treatment:* define each gear's
    model domain from **Stage 1 activity**, never from the whole series. A
    domain chosen from all stages would drop cells abandoned because of the
    projects, which conditions on the outcome.
14. **Autocorrelation in space and time.** Spatial autocorrelation is strong in
    every surface, and each cell is measured repeatedly over months.
    *Treatment:* every model carries a spatial random field or smooth plus a
    temporal term, and the residuals are tested for leftover autocorrelation.
15. **Multiple testing in the local statistics.** There are 3,376 tests per
    surface, across 2 datasets × 3 gears × 3 stages, plus the 2 seasons of the
    stage × season surfaces. *Treatment:*
    Benjamini–Hochberg FDR within each surface, with seeded conditional
    permutation.
16. **Gi\* cannot find cold spots at a floor of zero.** On AFE surfaces with
    40–95% zeros, a cell cannot sit significantly below a mean that is itself
    near zero. The archive already recorded this. *Treatment:* report it as a
    property of the statistic, not a finding (@sec-local).

### Regulatory

17. **Inside a safety zone, lost effort is mandated, not avoidance**
    (2026-10-20). The U.S. Coast Guard set a 500 m safety zone around every
    SFW, RWF and SRW foundation, from installation through turbine and
    platform construction (SFW enforced 2023-05-01 to 2024-05-31; RWF and SRW
    rules run to 2027 and 2028). Non-construction vessels are excluded there,
    so a fall in effort inside a zone is a regulatory effect. One zone covers
    about 0.79 km², most of a 0.93 km² cell, so at this grid's resolution the
    exclusion fills most of each foundation's own cell. *Treatment:*
    - `sz_share(t)`, the area share of each cell inside an active zone, is
      in the month and season-year tables (`05`), and enters the timing
      model as its own term, so *h*(·) and *λ* estimate the response
      **beyond** the mandated exclusion;
    - the stage × season BAG is also reported without the cells ever inside
      a zone, so the inside-band *γ* is not driven by mandated exclusion
      (@sec-sensitivity);
    - SFW's zones lapsed on 2024-05-31, leaving 27 months (June 2024 –
      August 2026) when fishing beside its turbines was legal again. Whether
      effort returns there is the cleanest test of **lasting** avoidance
      (@sec-bag);
    - the rules enforce the zones only during active construction (about
      48 h to 1 week per location for RWF and SRW, by Local Notice to
      Mariners), so `sz_share_install` (installation days only) is the
      enforcement-only lower bound, run as a sensitivity.

## Recommended treatments and transformations {#sec-treatments}

One principle runs through this section: **transform for descriptive spatial
statistics, never for the models.** The models fit raw hours with an
appropriate family and an exposure offset.

### Derived quantities (Phase 0)

| Field | Definition | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | hours ÷ months in the time step | Comparing stages |
| `n_mmsi_fleet` | Distinct Primary MMSIs per gear active anywhere in the AOI in the time step (a regional count if available) | Denominator of `rate_fleet`. Fleet-size sensitivity covariate (caveat 5) |
| `rate_fleet` | hours ÷ (months × `n_mmsi_fleet`) | Level comparisons only, reported next to `rate` to show AIS uptake (caveat 5). A constant per gear and time step, so it leaves the spatial statistics unchanged. Never a model response; the models take fleet size as a covariate or offset. |
| `density` | hours ÷ (months × `area_km2`) | Maps, descriptives (h km⁻² month⁻¹) |
| `log_expo` | `log(months × area_km2)` | Model offset |
| `y_vst` | Variance-stabilised density (below) | Moran's I, General G, LISA, Gi\* |
| `dist_lease_km` | Signed distance from cell centroid to the nearest lease boundary (negative inside) | BAG gradient |
| `dist_band` | `inside`, `0–2`, `2–4`, `4–8`, `8–15` km | BAG factor. At least 280 cells per band; 8–15 is the reference. |
| `nearest_project` | SFW / RWF / SRW | Project-specific gradients |
| `x_km`, `y_km` | Centroid in EPSG:32619, km | Spatial fields and the mesh |
| `moy`, `year`, `t_index` | Month of year, year, month index | Seasonality and trend |
| `season` | `AprSep` / `OctMar` | Stage × season and season-year tables (@sec-time-steps) |
| `season_year` | Year of the season, with Oct–Mar labelled by the year it ends in (Oct 2020 – Mar 2021 is 2021) | Season-year tables. The first (2016 `OctMar`, 3 months) and last (2026 `AprSep`, 5 months) are partial. |
| `months` | Months in the stage, stage × season stratum or season-year | Exposure in `log_expo` and in `rate`, so partial and unequal strata compare fairly |
| `rate_std` | Season-standardised stage rate: the mean of the 12 month-of-year mean rates within the stage | Level comparisons only (caveat 8) |
| `domain_{gear}` | Cell active for that gear in Stage 1 (VP or AFE > 0) | Model domain (@sec-caveats, item 13) |
| `depth_m`, `slope_deg`, `depth_sd_m`, `bpi_broad` | Per-cell bathymetry and terrain summaries | Static environmental covariates (@sec-env) |
| `habitat_*` | Per-cell habitat class shares, once the Ørsted data arrive | Static environmental covariates (@sec-env) |
| `d_found_final_km`, `d_cable_km` | Distance to the nearest eventual foundation (planned included) and to the nearest cable route | Static; an alternative BAG gradient measured to the structures rather than the lease line (@sec-infra) |
| `d_found_km`, `n_found_2km`, `active_construction`, `cable_works`, `phase`, `months_since_first_found` | Time-varying foundation and cable exposure (month tables; season-year means and shares) | Timing BAG (@sec-infra) |
| `sz_share`, `sz_share_install` | Share of the cell's area inside an active USCG 500 m safety zone: installation to rule end, and installation days only (month tables; season-year means) | Timing BAG term for mandated exclusion; sensitivity (caveat 17) |

### Environmental covariates: bathymetry and benthic habitat {#sec-env}

Depth and seabed type set *where* each gear fishes. Trawlers work soft
sediment at particular depths; pots and gillnets work hard bottom and edges.
Adding them to the models does three things:

- it explains part of the baseline spatial pattern;
- it makes the stationary SPDE field more plausible, since the field no longer
  has to absorb depth gradients;
- it sharpens the BAG contrast, by comparing cells of similar habitat at
  different distances from the turbines.

Both covariates are **static**. They cannot confound the period × distance
(BAG) interaction, which varies over time. They can be collinear with the
distance *main effect*, and with the spatial field (spatial confounding).
Phase 5 checks both (below).

#### Bathymetry: NCEI Coastal Relief Model Vol. 1 (2023)

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Source | NOAA NCEI U.S. Coastal Relief Model, Volume 1 (Northeast Atlantic), 2023 release, 1 arc-second (≈ 30 m), built from NCEI's CUDEM tiles. File `crm_vol1_2023.nc` (≈ 1.6 GB for the whole volume) in the THREDDS catalog `https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/thredds/catalog/crm/cudem/catalog.html` |
| Request | **Only the AOI bounding box plus a 5 km buffer**, via THREDDS (NetCDF Subset or OPeNDAP) or NCEI's grid-extract tool. Never the full volume. Record the exact request URL, access date and returned file hash in the provenance sidecar. |
| Vertical datum | EGM2008 (≈ mean sea level), metres, negative down. Convert to positive `depth_m` and record the datum. |
| Storage | `data/sf/bathy/crm_vol1_2023_aoi.tif` (GeoTIFF, EPSG:4326 as delivered), with a `.json` provenance sidecar. Written by `05`; nothing is edited by hand. |
| Licence | US Government work, public domain. Cite the DOI given on NCEI's record. |
| Fallback | GEBCO 2024 (15 arc-second) if CRM access fails. It is coarser than the 0.84 × 1.11 km cells but enough for mean depth. |

**Derived per-cell covariates** (in `05`, with `terra`):

1. Project the raster to EPSG:32619 with bilinear resampling (30 m).
2. Derive terrain layers at 30 m:
   - slope (`terra::terrain(v = "slope")`);
   - a **broad-scale bathymetric position index**: depth minus the focal mean
     in a 1–3 km annulus (`terra::focal`). It separates ridges and banks from
     troughs at the scale of the grid.
3. Summarise each layer to the grid cells with area-weighted extraction
   (`terra::extract(..., exact = TRUE)`): mean depth, SD of depth (a rugosity
   proxy), mean slope and mean BPI.
4. Checks:
   - every cell has a non-missing depth;
   - all depths are positive (the AOI does not touch land);
   - the range matches the CRM for the region;
   - a map of `depth_m` sits alongside the effort maps in `06`.

**Treatment in the models:**

- Centre and scale each covariate.
- Enter depth as a low-rank smooth (`s(depth_m, k = 4)`, or a quadratic in
  INLA), because gear-depth responses peak at intermediate depths.
- Enter slope / BPI linearly.
- Check collinearity with `dist_lease_km`: Spearman ρ, concurvity for
  `mgcv`-type smooths, VIF for linear terms.
- If |ρ| > 0.7, keep depth in the model and report that the distance *main*
  effect is not separately identified. The BAG interaction still is.

#### Benthic habitat: Ørsted classification (pending)

Ask Ørsted for the layer in this form, and log the request in the open items:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `geometry` | POLYGON, or a raster of classes | With its CRS |
| `habitat_class` | string | Ideally CMECS substrate classes (group / subgroup) as used in BOEM site characterisation, or Ørsted's own scheme with a crosswalk to CMECS |
| `survey`, `survey_date`, `method` | string / date | E.g. MBES + backscatter + grab / video ground truth |
| `confidence` | string / numeric | Classification confidence where available |
| *Coverage polygon* | POLYGON | **Essential**: the area actually surveyed |

**Coverage is the main risk.** Site-characterisation surveys usually cover the
lease areas and cable corridors, not the 10 km buffer. A covariate that exists
only inside the leases is perfectly confounded with being inside a lease, so
it cannot enter the full-AOI models. The rules:

1. **Covers ≥ 95% of the AOI:** add per-cell habitat shares (`habitat_*`,
   compositional; drop one reference class) as fixed effects in every model.
2. **Covers the leases and corridors only:**
   - use it *inside* the leases, to stratify the lease-level results (e.g.
     fixed-gear effort on hard vs soft bottom inside the arrays);
   - for the full-AOI models, use a regional substrate product with full
     coverage instead (USGS usSEABED sediment, or the sediment layers on the
     Northeast Ocean Data Portal);
   - run the Ørsted layer as a sensitivity on the covered cells.
3. Either way, record the class scheme and crosswalk in
   `references/data_dictionary.md`. Store the layer under `data/sf/habitat/`
   with the sharing terms noted in `references/`.

### Time steps {#sec-time-steps}

**Decision (2026-10-18, D-013, D-014):** one set of time steps for all descriptive work,
and model time steps that differ by gear only where the data require it.

**Seasons are Apr–Sep and Oct–Mar.** Both stage boundaries (2020-10-01 and
2023-04-01) fall between these seasons, so no stage × season stratum or
season-year straddles two stages. Apr–Sep also captures slightly more of the
fixed-gear peak than May–Sep does (80.5% against 78.3%). A four-season split
(Dec–Feb, Mar–May, Jun–Aug, Sep–Nov) would break both stage boundaries; it is
kept as a sensitivity (@sec-sensitivity).

**Months per stage × season stratum:**

| Stage | Apr–Sep | Oct–Mar |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 30 | 27 |
| 2 | 12 | 18 |
| 3 | 23 | 18 |

**Coarser steps reduce the zeros, but do not remove them.** Share of
cell-step values that are zero, within each gear's Stage 1 domain (caveat 13):

| AFE time step | Steps per cell | MOBILE | FIXED | POLE_AND_LINE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Month | 128 | 96.3% | 97.7% | 97.1% |
| Season (4 per year) | 43 | 90.4% | 94.4% | 93.0% |
| Season-year (Apr–Sep / Oct–Mar) | 22 | 83.5% | 90.0% | 87.1% |
| Year | 11 | 70.4% | 81.7% | 78.4% |

Pooling cannot create vessels. The zeros come from the few vessels logging
fishing (caveat 12), and the model families already handle zero shares this
high. What the step changes is how well the models can be fitted and how
precisely construction timing is resolved.

**Positive cell-steps available to the models**, within the Stage 1 domain:

| | Month | Season-year | Stage × season |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AFE MOBILE (1,613 cells) | 7,648 | 5,861 | 4,246 |
| AFE FIXED (465 cells) | 1,381 | 1,018 | 802 |
| AFE POLE_AND_LINE (162 cells) | 596 | 461 | 318 |
| VP MOBILE | 45,470 | 26,923 | 13,459 |
| VP FIXED | 14,679 | 11,517 | 7,861 |
| VP POLE_AND_LINE | 5,072 | 4,408 | 3,312 |

**Descriptive steps (all gears and datasets):**

| Step | Surfaces per dataset × gear | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Stage (default) | 3 | Global and local statistics, maps, change classes |
| Stage × season | 6 | The same statistics, comparing stages within one season; the fair view of stage change (caveats 8–9) |
| Season-year | 22 | Time series of Moran's I and of effort; replaces the monthly I(t), which is erratic at 96–98% zeros |

Spatial statistics change with temporal aggregation, because longer
periods smooth the surface and raise Moran's I. Stage 2 mobile VP, for
example, gives I = 0.70 over all 30 months and 0.63 over its 12 Apr–Sep
months. A shared step keeps differences between gears from being artefacts
of the step. Monthly series stay in use for display (time-series plots), not
for spatial statistics.

**Model steps:**

| Model | VP (all gears) | AFE MOBILE | AFE FIXED | AFE POLE_AND_LINE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary BAG (shared, comparable across gears) | Cell × stage × season | Cell × stage × season | Cell × stage × season | Not modelled |
| Timing model (Ørsted dates, turbine distance) | Cell × month | Cell × month; season-year as a sensitivity | Cell × season-year | Not modelled |

- **Mobile AFE stays monthly:** its effort is spread through the year, so
  pooling would discard real seasonal signal, and 7,648 positives are enough
  for a monthly hurdle model.
- **Fixed AFE moves to season-year:** with 1,381 positives over 465 cells,
  monthly occupancy is too sparse for a stable binomial part (and for the
  Laplace approximation in INLA, Phase 5 condition 5). Most of its off-season
  months are near-certain zeros.
- **What season-year costs:** exposure onset is blurred by up to five months.
  The time-varying covariates for season-year models are the mean over the
  season's months (distances, counts) and the share of months (construction
  and cable-works flags), written by `02a` to `infra_cell_season_year.csv`
  and the season-year tables (@sec-infra). The blur matters most for SRW,
  whose foundations went in over Jun–Oct 2025, across both seasons.
- **Pole-and-line AFE** is limited by vessels, not by the time step: 162
  domain cells, and one vessel holds 40% of its hours. No step rescues it.

### Variance-stabilising transforms for the spatial statistics

The Tweedie variance function Var(Y) ∝ μ^*p* is stabilised by
Y^(1 − *p*/2). Using the measured powers:

| Dataset | *p* | Stabilising exponent | Recommended |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| VP | ≈ 1.2 | ≈ 0.4 | **√ density** (Anscombe-like for counts). Matches the archived analysis, so the results stay comparable. |
| AFE | ≈ 1.7 | ≈ 0.15 | **log(density + *c*)**, with *c* = half the smallest positive density in that surface |

- Avoid `log1p(density)`. Densities are around 0.01–1 h km⁻² month⁻¹, and
  `log1p` of values that small is close to the identity, so it stabilises
  nothing. A log with a stated, data-derived constant is reproducible and
  scale-aware.
- Moran's I and Gi\* are invariant to multiplying the whole surface by a
  constant. Within one stage, √(hours) and √(density) give the same statistic,
  but log does not, which is why *c* is defined per surface.
- Sensitivity: raw density and the alternative transform (√ for AFE, log for
  VP) for every global and local statistic.

### Response families for the models

| Response | Family | Why |
|---|---|---|
| VP, cell × stage × season | **Negative binomial (NB2)**, log link, with a season term | Integer, overdispersed (var/mean 3–26), few zeros for mobile |
| VP, cell × month | **NB2**. Hurdle-NB if DHARMa flags excess zeros (likely for fixed and pole-and-line). | 89–98% zeros. NB alone may fit mobile. |
| AFE, cell × stage × season | **Tweedie** (*p* estimated) *vs* **delta-Gamma**, with a season term | Continuous with exact zeros. *p* ≈ 1.7. |
| AFE, cell × month (mobile) / cell × season-year (fixed) | **Delta-Gamma / delta-lognormal** (hurdle) | 84–97% zeros within the domain. Occupancy and intensity probably respond differently near turbines (@sec-models). |

### Scope per gear

Every gear and dataset gets the full descriptive treatment at all three
descriptive time steps (@sec-time-steps). The table covers the models.

| Gear | VP stage × season | VP timing | AFE stage × season | AFE timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOBILE | Full | Monthly | Full | Monthly (season-year sensitivity) |
| FIXED | Full | Monthly | Full | Season-year, domain-restricted |
| POLE_AND_LINE | Full | Monthly | **Not modelled.** Descriptive and spatial statistics only. | **Not modelled.** Only 601 cells were ever positive, and one vessel holds 40% of the hours. |

Each gear is modelled **separately**. A joint gear-interaction model is fitted
only to test formally whether the BAG effect differs between mobile and fixed
gear (@sec-models).

## Workflow overview {#sec-workflow}

New qmds continue the numbered `r/` sequence and the conventions already in
place:

- Every path goes in `r/paths.R`, with a Quarto-parameter override.
- Shared code lives in a sourced helper file with `testthat` tests.
- The setup chunk finds the repo root.
- Each qmd ends with `sessionInfo()` and `renv::diagnostics()`.
- No absolute paths, and no typed statistics in prose.

| Step | File | Phase | Writes (gitignored) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 02a | `02a_infrastructure.qmd` | 0: Ørsted turbines and cables → time-varying covariates (split out of `05`, decision 2026-10-28, D-060) | `data/sf/infra/`, `data/processed/analysis/infra_cell_*.csv` |
| 05 | `05_prepare_analysis.qmd` | 0: analysis tables, covariates, weights; joins 02a's covariates | `data/processed/analysis/` |
| 06 | `06_explore.qmd` | 1: EDA | figures, tables |
| 07 | `07_spatial_global.qmd` | 2: Global Moran's I, General G, correlograms | `spatial/global_*.csv` |
| 08 | `08_spatial_local.qmd` | 3: Local Moran's I vs Gi\*, change classes | `spatial/local_*.gpkg` |
| 09 | — | *Unused: the infrastructure step was folded into `05` (decision 2026-10-19, D-021), then split out as `02a` (D-060); the number is left unused so the later files keep theirs* | — |
| 10 | `10_bag.qmd` | 4: BAG models | `models/bag_*.rds` |
| 11 | `11_models_frequentist.qmd` | 5: Tweedie and hurdle GLMMs (`glmmTMB`, `sdmTMB`) | `models/freq_*.rds` |
| 12 | `12_models_inla.qmd` | 6: INLA-SPDE | `models/inla_*.rds` |
| 13 | `13_sensitivity.qmd` | 7: sensitivity grid | `sensitivity/*.csv` |
| 14 | `14_synthesis.qmd` | 8: results and figures for the thesis | `reports/figures/` |

Shared code: `r/analysis_helpers.R` (derived fields, weights, transforms,
domain flags, the model cache), `r/infra_helpers.R` (foundation CSVs,
date and coordinate parsing, exposure covariates) and `r/spatial_helpers.R` (wrappers for
global and local statistics, change classes). Each gets a test file in
`r/tests/testthat/`.

**Runtime and caching.** R renders are not frozen (see `r/_quarto.yml`), and
the INLA and spatiotemporal models can take hours. The helper
`fit_cached(key_inputs, fit_fun)` hashes the model formula, the input table and
the package versions with `digest` (already in `renv.lock`). It saves the fit
to `data/processed/models/<hash>.rds` with a JSON metadata sidecar, and re-fits
only when the hash changes. This avoids adding `targets` as a dependency. If
the pipeline grows past this, `targets` is the next step.

**New dependencies.** Approved on 2026-10-18 to add phase by phase. Install
each one when its phase starts and record it with `renv::snapshot()` in the
same commit as the code that first uses it.

| Package | Phase | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spdep` | 2–3 | already in renv | Weights, Moran's I, General G, `localmoran_perm`, `localG_perm` |
| `terra` | 0 | CRAN | Bathymetry subset, reprojection, terrain derivatives, area-weighted extraction (@sec-env) |
| `mgcv` | 5–6 | **pinned 2026-10-18** (1.9-3) | Cyclic smooths, the GAM alternative |
| `glmmTMB` | 5–6 | CRAN | Tweedie, NB2 and hurdle GLMMs |
| `DHARMa` | 5–7 | CRAN | Simulation-based residual diagnostics |
| `sdmTMB` | 6 | CRAN | SPDE random fields with Tweedie and delta families, spatial-block CV |
| `fmesher` | 6–7 | CRAN | SPDE meshes, shared by `sdmTMB` and `INLA` |
| `marginaleffects` | 5–6 | CRAN | Marginal predictions and contrasts from the two hurdle parts |
| `INLA` | 7 | **not on CRAN**: `https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable` | Bayesian SPDE |
| `inlabru` | 7 (optional) | CRAN | Simpler syntax for joint hurdle likelihoods |

## Phase 0: Analysis tables, covariates and weights (`05_prepare_analysis.qmd`) {#sec-phase0}

**Goal.** A tidy, documented analysis table per dataset × time step, keyed on
`cell_id`, with every derived field from @sec-treatments and saved weights.

**Steps**

1. Read the four gear tables. Filter to `set == "primary"` and drop the
   `UNRESOLVED` rows, after asserting they sum to 0 h. Keep Strict in a
   separate object for `13`.
2. Join the grid attributes (`area_km2`, `aoi_class`, centroid `x_km`/`y_km`)
   and the stage lengths from `dev_stages`.
3. Compute the derived fields: `rate`, `density`, `log_expo`, `y_vst`, `moy`,
   `year`, `t_index`, `season`, `season_year` and `months`.
   - Build the **stage × season** and **season-year** tables by summing the
     zero-filled monthly table. Do not re-aggregate from records, so the
     hours reconcile exactly with 04.
   - Compute `rate_std` for the stage tables (caveat 8).
   - Compute `n_mmsi_fleet` per gear and time step from the Primary rows of
     `gfw_{vp,afe}_id_classified.csv`. The cell tables carry no MMSI, and
     summing per-cell counts would count a vessel once for every cell it
     visits. Then compute `rate_fleet` for the stage tables (caveat 5).
4. Compute lease distances. Reproject the three leases to 32619, then derive
   the signed distance, `dist_band` and `nearest_project`.
5. Compute the domain flags `domain_{gear}` from Stage 1 only.
6. Bathymetry (@sec-env):
   - fetch the AOI subset of `crm_vol1_2023.nc`, with a hash check and
     provenance sidecar; skip the fetch if the stored file's hash matches;
   - derive slope and BPI;
   - extract the per-cell summaries and join them to `cells.gpkg`.

   Habitat shares are added in the same step once the Ørsted layer arrives.
7. Weights:
   - Rebuild queen contiguity both ways (02's `poly2nb()` and the lattice from
     `ix`/`iy`) and assert they are identical.
   - Assert 1 component, no islands and a mean above 7.7.
   - Write the neighbour list as a GAL file (`spdep::write.nb.gal`), which is
     interoperable with GeoDa and PySAL.
   - Build two weights objects: `lw_W` (row-standardised, for Moran's I and
     LISA) and `lw_B_self` (binary, self-inclusive, for General G and Gi\*).
8. Ørsted infrastructure (@sec-infra):
   - read the RWF, SRW and SFW foundation CSVs, the SFW PSO dates (as a
     check) and the three layout GeoJSONs; collapse each foundation's
     installation-day rows to its first and last day; match CSV positions to
     layout points (RWF by grid name, SRW and SFW by distance) and check each
     within 100 m; assert SFW's dates equal PSO Table 3;
   - write `data/sf/infra/infrastructure.gpkg` (layers `foundations`,
     `cables`) with a sidecar;
   - derive the per cell × month exposure covariates and their season-year
     aggregates, plus the SRW-planned sensitivity table; assert that
     exposure only grows over time.
9. Write `data/processed/analysis/{vp,afe}_{stage,stage_season,season_year,month}_gear.csv`,
   `cells.gpkg` (geometry plus static covariates, including bathymetry and the
   distances to the eventual foundations and cable routes) and the
   `infra_cell_*.csv` covariate tables, each with a JSON provenance sidecar
   (@sec-fair). The month and season-year tables carry the time-varying
   infrastructure covariates.

```{r}
#| label: phase0-weights
# Phase 0, step 7 (05_prepare_analysis.qmd): build the spatial weights used by
# every spatial statistic in Phases 2–3 and write them out once.
#
# Inputs:  `grid`, the fishnet from 02 (data/sf/fishnet/gfw_grid_utm19n.gpkg),
#          one row per cell with `cell_id` and its integer column/row indices
#          `ix`/`iy`; `paths` from r/paths.R.
# Outputs: `lw_W`, `lw_B_self` in memory, and grid_queen.gal in
#          data/processed/analysis/ for GeoDa/PySAL users (FAIR: interoperable).
#
# Why two independent neighbour builds: 02 builds contiguity from polygon
# geometry (`poly2nb`), which can silently drop or add links if cell edges
# carry floating-point slivers. The grid is a regular lattice, so neighbours
# can also be derived from the integer indices alone. If both agree, the
# weights are trustworthy whatever the geometry quirks.
library(spdep)

# Queen neighbours from lattice indices: cell i's neighbours are the up-to-8
# cells whose (ix, iy) differ by at most 1 in each direction, excluding itself.
# Cells missing from the grid (the AOI is irregular) simply do not match.
lattice_nb <- function(ix, iy, ids) {
  # Lookup from "ix iy" string to row position, so candidates resolve in O(1)
  key <- setNames(seq_along(ix), paste(ix, iy))
  nb <- lapply(seq_along(ix), function(i) {
    # All 9 positions in the 3 x 3 block centred on cell i (including i)
    cand <- paste(ix[i] + rep(-1:1, 3), iy[i] + rep(-1:1, each = 3))
    j <- unname(key[cand])
    # Drop positions outside the grid (NA) and the cell itself; spdep expects
    # sorted integer row positions
    sort(as.integer(j[!is.na(j) & j != i]))
  })
  # Assemble a valid spdep "nb" object with the same attributes poly2nb sets
  structure(nb, class = "nb", region.id = ids, type = "queen", sym = TRUE)
}

# snap = 0: cells must share an exact vertex or edge; the grid from 02 is
# exact, so any tolerance would only hide a construction error
nb_poly    <- poly2nb(grid, queen = TRUE, snap = 0)
nb_lattice <- lattice_nb(grid$ix, grid$iy, grid$cell_id)

# Gate checks (Phase 0 gate):
#  - both builds give identical links (attributes such as call differ, so ignore them);
#  - one connected component, so every permutation test is defined over the
#    whole AOI and no sub-region is tested in isolation;
#  - no islands, i.e. no cell with zero neighbours, which would break row
#    standardisation and local statistics;
#  - mean neighbour count above 7.7 (measured 7.80): a drop would mean cells
#    were lost from the grid
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(nb_poly, nb_lattice, check.attributes = FALSE)),
          n.comp.nb(nb_poly)$nc == 1, all(card(nb_poly) > 0),
          mean(card(nb_poly)) > 7.7)

# Two weighting schemes, each matched to the statistic's definition:
#  - row-standardised ("W"): Moran's I and local Moran's I (LISA) compare a
#    cell with the *average* of its neighbours, so edge cells with fewer
#    neighbours are not down-weighted;
#  - binary with the cell itself included ("B" + include.self): Gi* is defined
#    as the share of the total in a cell's neighbourhood *including* the cell.
#    General G uses binary weights without self (built in Phase 2).
lw_W      <- nb2listw(nb_poly, style = "W")                # Moran's I, LISA
lw_B_self <- nb2listw(include.self(nb_poly), style = "B")  # Gi*

# Persist the neighbour list as GAL, the plain-text format GeoDa and PySAL read,
# so the exact weights behind every reported statistic can be reused
write.nb.gal(nb_poly, file.path(paths$analysis, "grid_queen.gal"))
```

**Gate.** All assertions pass. Hours in each analysis table equal hours in the
interim table, per gear × time step, and the stage × season and season-year
tables sum to the monthly totals. No stage × season stratum or season-year
spans two stages. The infrastructure layers match their sources (13 / 68 / 85
foundation positions; 13 / 68 / 45 installed by August 2026), every
foundation lies in its own lease, and no cell's exposure ever decreases.
SFW's dates equal PSO Table 3, and each SFW `USCG_ID` names its matched
position. Safety-zone shares lie in [0, 1], none precedes the first
foundation (June 2023), no foundation predates its project's zone rule,
and SFW's zones lapse from June 2024.

## Phase 1: Exploratory analysis (`06_explore.qmd`) {#sec-phase1}

**Goal.** Recompute everything in @sec-structure at render time, and test the
assumptions the later phases rest on.

**Steps**

1. **Composition.** Hours, records and MMSIs by gear × stage × dataset, raw
   and season-standardised (caveat 8), and by stage × season.
2. **Distribution diagnostics** per dataset × gear at each descriptive time
   step (stage, stage × season, season-year) and per month:
   - percent zero, mean, variance, var/mean, skewness;
   - quantiles of the positive values;
   - Tweedie power by the log-variance/log-mean slope, and by profile
     likelihood (`glmmTMB` fits with *p* free, once installed);
   - for VP, check that `vp_hours` is integer.
3. **Transform check.** Compare four scales for every surface: raw density,
   √, log(density + *c*) and the chosen `y_vst`. This confirms or overrides
   the choices in @sec-treatments.

   The transforms serve only the spatial statistics, which are tested by
   permutation. Normality is therefore not the goal. What matters is that the
   variance stops growing with the mean, and that a few extreme cells do not
   dominate. The models never see the transformed values (they fit raw hours).
   With 40–99% zeros in many surfaces, no transform makes a surface normal.
   So every plot uses the **positive values only, with the surface's zero
   share printed on each panel**.

   Numbers, per surface and scale:
   - skewness of the positive values;
   - the mean–variance slope across cells (log variance on log mean, as in
     step 2), computed on the transformed values;
   - the share of high-leverage cells in the Moran scatterplot (below).

   Plots, one faceted page per dataset × time step (stage, stage × season,
   season-year), with gear × stratum as rows and the four scales as columns,
   so the 36 stage × season surfaces fit on two pages rather than 144 plots:
   1. **Distribution:** histograms or density plots of the positive values.
   2. **Spread:** a mean–variance plot across cells on log–log axes with the
      fitted slope. A flat line on the transformed scale means the variance
      is stabilised.
   3. **Normality (supporting only):** QQ plots of the positive values against
      the normal.
   4. **Relationships:** density against `depth_m`, `dist_lease_km` and
      `bpi_broad`, with a loess smooth. This shows whether a transform
      straightens a relationship or hides it, which matters for reading the
      local statistics against distance in Phase 3.
   5. **Influence on the spatial statistics:** a Moran scatterplot per
      surface (`spdep::moran.plot` with `lw_W`), raw against `y_vst`.
      High-leverage cells are those flagged by its influence measures (hat
      value or Cook's distance). This links the transform choice to the
      statistics it serves.

   Write the per-surface numbers to `tables/transform_check_{vp,afe}.csv` and
   the pages to `figures/transform_check_{vp,afe}_{timestep}.png`.

   **Decision rule.** Keep the transform in @sec-treatments (√ for VP,
   log(density + *c*) for AFE) unless the alternative does better on the
   median surface of a dataset × gear by **both** of:
   - the mean–variance slope is at least 0.2 closer to zero;
   - the share of high-leverage cells is at least a third lower.

   Report the result either way. A switch applies to that dataset × gear at
   every time step, so the gears stay comparable within a time step, and the
   rejected transform becomes the Phase 3 robustness run.
4. **Time series.** Monthly Primary VP and AFE by gear, split inside/outside
   the leases and by `dist_band`, with the stage boundaries marked and each
   project's foundation window shaded (SFW Jun–Aug 2023, RWF May 2024 – Aug
   2025, SRW Jun–Oct 2025). Include STL or cyclic-smooth decompositions of
   trend and season.
5. **Vessel concentration and the pre-window screen.**
   - Lorenz curves and top-*k* shares per gear × stage.
   - Profile any vessel holding more than 10% of a gear × stage total.
   - For every hull with a charter or survey window, compare the share of its
     hours inside the leases in the 12 months before the window with the
     fleet's share. Flag hulls more than twice the fleet share, if they have
     at least 20 pre-window hours (a share on fewer is noise). PROVIDER is
     the current case (caveat 11).
6. **Depth and effort.** Effort density against `depth_m` and BPI per gear.
   Check the expected gear–depth niches, and the collinearity of depth with
   `dist_lease_km`.
7. **Is AIS uptake spatially uniform?** (The key BAG assumption.) Plot the
   trend in active MMSIs per `dist_band` per gear, and in the all-vessel raw VP
   per band (`gfw_vp_id_cell_month.csv`). Do the bands rise in parallel
   *before* construction (Stages 1–2)? Test with a `band × year` interaction
   restricted to Stages 1–2. (Stages 1–2 end before SFW's first works in
   March 2023, so they are pre-construction for every project. The Phase 4
   equivalence test extends each cell's pre-period to its nearest project's
   first works, @sec-bag-pretrend.)
8. **Maps.** Density maps per gear × stage and per gear × stage × season, on
   one shared colour scale per gear and dataset, with the lease outlines, the
   foundation positions (installed filled, SRW planned hollow) and the n_MMSI
   per cell. Reuse the committed basemap rasters in
   `references/basemap/`. Maps of differences between stages use
   season-standardised rates, or compare within one season (caveat 8).
9. **Temporal completeness** per cell × gear (active months / 128, and active
   season-years / 22). This confirms the model time steps in
   @sec-time-steps: monthly for VP and mobile AFE, season-year for fixed AFE.
10. **Construction exposure and event time** (descriptive groundwork for
    Phase 4 steps 1–2, needs the `02a` covariates):
    - a map of every foundation coloured by installation quarter, with the
      cable routes by type;
    - cells per month reached by each covariate (`n_found_2km > 0`,
      `active_construction`, `cable_works`), by nearest project, which shows
      how much exposure contrast the timing model has;
    - mean density by band against `months_since_first_found` (−24 to +24),
      per dataset × gear × project.

**Gate.**

- Step 3 confirms the transform for each dataset × gear, or switches it under
  the decision rule. Update `y_vst` in `05` and re-render before Phase 2.
- Step 7 shows parallel pre-construction trends across bands → proceed with the
  within-AOI BAG.
- If not, add a `band × year` pre-trend term to every BAG model and say so.
- Any hull flagged in step 5 goes back to `03` for a decision before the
  Stage 1 baseline is used for inference. PROVIDER was the first case and was
  resolved on 2026-10-18 (caveat 11).

## Phase 2: Global spatial autocorrelation (`07_spatial_global.qmd`) {#sec-global}

**Goal.** Measure how much each surface clusters, how that changes across
stages and months, and the spatial scale of the clustering. The scale feeds the
Phase 3 weights and the SPDE range priors.

**Statistics**

| Statistic | Weights | Detects | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Moran's I** | `lw_W` | Similar values together, high or low | `moran.mc(nsim = 999)`, seeded. Report I with a permutation 95% interval, not just p. |
| **Getis-Ord General G** | binary (`style = "B"`), no self | Whether *high* values cluster more than low ones | Needs non-negative values, which holds. `globalG.test()`. Read with Moran's I: a high I with an unremarkable G means the low values drive the clustering. |
| *(optional)* Geary's C | `lw_W` | Local differences | A cross-check on Moran's I |

**Steps**

1. Moran's I and General G on `y_vst` for each dataset × gear × stage
   (18 surfaces) and each dataset × gear × stage × season (36 surfaces), plus
   the raw-density sensitivity. Every gear and dataset uses the same steps
   (@sec-time-steps).
2. Moran's I **per season-year** (22 steps) for each dataset × gear. Plot I(t)
   with the stage boundaries, with Apr–Sep and Oct–Mar as separate series. Is
   clustering itself changing as construction goes on? Season-year replaces
   monthly I(t), which is erratic at 96–98% zeros.
3. **Correlograms.** Moran's I by contiguity order 1–10 (`sp.correlogram`)
   and by distance band (0–2, 2–4, … 20 km). The distance where I falls to
   about 0.1 gives:
   - the candidate neighbourhood for the Phase 3 weight sensitivity;
   - an empirical prior for the Matérn range in Phase 6 (*ρ*₀).
4. Summary figure: I and G z by gear × stage, with the stage × season values
   alongside. Season standardisation is not used here: these statistics do
   not change when a surface is multiplied by a constant (caveat 8).

```{r}
#| label: phase2-global
# Phase 2, step 1 (07_spatial_global.qmd): global clustering tests for one
# surface (one dataset x gear x time step). Called on `y_vst` for the 18
# stage surfaces and the 36 stage x season surfaces, then again on raw density
# as a sensitivity. The same function serves the season-year series (step 2).
#
# The two tests answer different questions, which is why both are run:
#  - Moran's I: do similar values sit next to each other (high-high AND
#    low-low)? It is symmetric in highs and lows.
#  - General G: are the *high* values concentrated together? It ignores
#    low-low clustering, so it speaks directly to "is effort clumped".
#
# Inputs: `y_I` (values for Moran's I) and `y_G` (non-negative values for
#         General G), numeric vectors in the same row order as the grid (and
#         hence the weights); `lw_W` and `lw_B` from Phase 0 / below.
# Output: one-row tibble, bound across surfaces into the Phase 2 summary table.

# Fixed seed so permutation p-values reproduce exactly (FAIR: reusable)
set.seed(42)

global_stats <- function(y_I, lw_W, lw_B, y_G = y_I) {
  # Permutation test: values are shuffled across cells 999 times, keeping the
  # weights fixed. With skewed, zero-heavy surfaces (caveats 1–3) this is safer
  # than the normal approximation.
  mi <- moran.mc(y_I, lw_W, nsim = 999)
  # General G has no permutation variant in spdep; its z-test is analytical.
  # It requires non-negative values. That holds for raw density and for VP's
  # y_vst (√density), but NOT for AFE's y_vst, log(density + c), which is
  # negative wherever density < c, including every zero cell. So G takes
  # `y_G`: √density for VP, and log(1 + density / c) = y_vst − log(c) for AFE,
  # y_vst shifted so a zero cell is exactly 0 (decision 2026-10-20, D-027). Moran's I
  # is unchanged by adding a constant, so I and G still read the same surface.
  # In r/07 this is global_stats(y_I, lw_W, lw_B, y_G = g_scale(density, ds)).
  gg <- globalG.test(y_G, lw_B)
  # mi$res holds the 999 permuted statistics followed by the observed one, so
  # drop the last element to get the null distribution alone. Its 2.5–97.5%
  # range is the band I would fall in with no spatial structure: a reference
  # band, not a confidence interval for I.
  null_I <- head(mi$res, -1)
  tibble(I = mi$statistic,
         I_null_lo = quantile(null_I, .025), I_null_hi = quantile(null_I, .975),
         I_p = mi$p.value,
         G = gg$estimate[1],       # observed General G
         G_z = gg$statistic,       # standard deviate vs expectation under no clustering
         G_p = gg$p.value)
}

# General G uses binary weights without the cell itself, per Getis & Ord
# (1992); the self-inclusive version is reserved for local Gi* (Phase 3)
lw_B <- nb2listw(nb_poly, style = "B")
```

(`mi$res` is the permutation reference distribution under the null, so its
quantiles give a no-clustering reference band rather than an interval for I.
The interval for I itself comes from a cell-block bootstrap, which is cheap.)

**Gate.**

- Correlogram range below about 3 km → queen weights are adequate.
- Range above about 5 km → add a distance-band weights run to Phase 3.
- Range of 3–5 km (borderline, decision 2026-10-20, D-028) → queen stays primary,
  and the distance-band run is added as well, at the range rounded up to a
  whole km.
- Range censored (I still ≥ 0.1 at 20 km) → counts as above 5 km.
- Every distance-band run is capped at 10 km, censored or not, so the band
  never approaches the AOI's width.
- *ρ*₀ per dataset × gear is the median of its three stage ranges
  (censored if two or more are). Write it to `global_rho0.csv` and its
  provenance sidecar for Phase 6.

## Phase 3: Local Moran's I vs Getis-Ord Gi\* (`08_spatial_local.qmd`) {#sec-local}

**Goal.** Compare the two local statistics on these data using pre-specified
criteria, then adopt one as the primary hotspot method, with the other in a
defined supporting role.

### What each statistic answers

| | Local Moran's I (LISA) | Getis-Ord Gi\* |
|---|---|---|
| Question | Is this cell similar to, or different from, its neighbours? | Is the neighbourhood sum, including the cell, unusually high or low? |
| Output | HH, LL, HL, LH clusters and outliers | Hot / cold, z-score |
| Weights | Row-standardised (`lw_W`) | Binary, self-inclusive (`lw_B_self`). The archive found that row-standardised Gi\* gives zero hotspots. |
| Inference | Conditional permutation (`localmoran_perm`) | Analytic z, or permutation (`localG_perm`). On skewed data the analytic normal approximation is poor, so **use permutation.** |
| Weak point here | LL in empty sea means nothing, and outliers are unstable in sparse surfaces | No cold spots at a floor of zero (caveat 16), and no outlier class |

### Comparison criteria

All criteria are fixed before the results are seen.

1. **Agreement.** Cohen's κ between Gi\* hot and LISA HH (and between cold and
   LL) per surface, with maps of the cells where they disagree.
2. **Behaviour on zero-inflated surfaces.** The share of significant LL / cold
   cells that are all-zero neighbourhoods. A statistic that labels empty sea
   "significant" is not informative about effort.
3. **Unique information.** How many HL / LH outliers there are and where:
   - inside the leases (isolated high fixed-gear cells next to turbines);
   - on lease boundaries.
   Gi\* cannot give this.
4. **Stability.** For each statistic, the share of runs in which a cell keeps
   its significant class across:
   - the leave-one-vessel-out jackknife (top 10 MMSIs per gear, re-aggregated
     from the record-level file);
   - permutation seeds;
   - weights: queen vs second-order queen vs distance band (from Phase 2).
5. **Detection power on a known signal.** Plant synthetic signals in null
   surfaces simulated from the Phase 5 base model, which keeps the observed
   zero structure and autocorrelation. *Until Phase 5 exists (decision
   2026-10-20, D-038):* interim nulls, a Gaussian random field at each gear's *ρ*₀
   rank-mapped onto the observed Stage 1 values; re-run with Phase 5
   simulations when they exist. The planted signals:
   - a 2-km "avoidance halo" (–50% inside the leases);
   - a "spillover ring" (+50% at 2–4 km).
   Measure sensitivity and false-positive rate for each statistic after FDR.
   This is the most direct measure of efficacy for *this* question.
6. **Stage-change readability.** Do the change classes (`gained hot`,
   `lost hot`, …) from each method line up with the BAG estimates from Phase 4?
   Agreement with the model is the external validation. *Deferred until
   Phase 4 has run; the primary-method choice stays provisional until then.*

### Steps

1. Run `localmoran_perm(nsim = 999, iseed = 42)` on `y_vst` and
   `localG_perm(nsim = 999, iseed = 42)` on the non-negative G scale
   (`g_scale()`) for each dataset × gear × stage, and for each dataset × gear
   × stage × season. Use the **z-moment permutation p-values**
   (`Pr(z != E(Ii))`, `Pr(z != E(Gi))`; decision 2026-10-20, D-036). Apply BH-FDR
   within each surface at q = 0.05 and q = 0.10.
2. Build classes:
   - Gi\* bins −3…+3 (99/95/90%), as in the archive;
   - LISA quadrants (`attr(., "quadr")$mean`) where the FDR-adjusted p
     clears q.
3. Stage-change classes S1→S2, S2→S3 and S1→S3, from the stage surfaces and
   **within each season** (Apr–Sep S1 → Apr–Sep S2, and so on). The
   within-season classes are the ones free of the calendar-mix confound
   (caveat 8). Keep the archived mutually exclusive scheme so results compare
   with the poster, and report the area (km²) in each class by `dist_band`.
4. Score criteria 1–6 and write a comparison table.
5. Decide the primary method.

```{r}
#| label: phase3-local
# Phase 3, steps 1–2 (08_spatial_local.qmd): local clustering for one surface,
# run with both methods so they can be scored against criteria 1–6.
#
# Inputs:  `y` (y_vst for one dataset x gear x stage, or x stage x season;
#          grid row order) for LISA, and `y_G` (g_scale(density), the
#          non-negative G scale) for Gi*; `lw_W` and `lw_B_self` from Phase 0.
#          As built in r/08 (local_stats() in r/spatial_helpers.R).
# Outputs: per-cell statistics and class labels, later joined to cells.gpkg
#          for mapping and for the stage-change classes (step 3).

# Local Moran's I (LISA): row-standardised weights, as in the global test.
# Conditional permutation: each cell's value is held fixed while the others
# are shuffled 999 times. `iseed` makes the parallel-safe RNG reproducible.
# Two-sided, because both clusters (high-high, low-low) and outliers
# (high-low, low-high) are of interest.
lisa <- localmoran_perm(y, lw_W, nsim = 999, iseed = 42, alternative = "two.sided")

# Getis-Ord Gi*: binary weights including the cell itself, so the statistic
# measures how much of the total sits in the cell's 3 x 3 neighbourhood.
# Same permutation design, so the two methods differ only in the statistic.
# localG_perm() computes Gi* as a share of the surface total, so it needs
# non-negative values: AFE's log y_vst would reverse the sign of every z.
gi   <- localG_perm(y_G, lw_B_self, nsim = 999, iseed = 42, alternative = "two.sided")

# Classification (caveat 15). With 3,376 cells tested at once, unadjusted
# p < 0.05 would flag about 170 cells by chance alone. Benjamini–Hochberg FDR
# controls the expected share of false discoveries within each surface.
# p-values: the z-moment permutation p (each cell's statistic against its own
# permutation mean and variance; no floor). Not the rank p ("... Sim"), whose
# floor of 2/1,000 left the sparse AFE surfaces with no rejections, and not
# the folded p, which spdep 1.4.2 gets wrong for Gi* on empty neighbourhoods
# (decision 2026-10-20, D-036).
# LISA classes: High-High, Low-Low, High-Low, Low-High where significant
lisa_sig <- p.adjust(lisa[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"], "BH") <= 0.05
lisa_class <- ifelse(lisa_sig, as.character(attr(lisa, "quadr")$mean), "ns")
# Gi* classes: hot or cold spot, by the sign of (Gi − E.Gi). On zero-floored
# AFE surfaces cold spots are largely undetectable (caveat 16), so read their
# absence with care. The 99/95/90% bins (-3…+3) come from the same adjusted
# p-values at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (step 2). Note: the internals column
# labelled "StdDev.Gi" holds this z, not a standard deviation.
g_int <- attr(gi, "internals")
gi_z <- (g_int[, "Gi"] - g_int[, "E.Gi"]) / sqrt(g_int[, "Var.Gi"])
gi_sig <- p.adjust(g_int[, "Pr(z != E(Gi))"], "BH") <= 0.05
gi_class <- ifelse(gi_sig, ifelse(gi_z > 0, "hot", "cold"), "ns")
```

**Expected outcome, to be confirmed by the criteria.**

- **Gi\* is primary** for hotspot mapping and stage-change classes: it is
  stable on sparse surfaces and reads directly as "where is effort
  concentrated".
- **LISA is secondary**, for its HL/LH outliers inside and next to the leases,
  which is where turbine-associated fixed-gear activity would show.
- LL and Gi\* cold results on AFE are reported as uninformative by
  construction.

**Gate.** If the criterion-5 power for a 2-km halo is below about 0.5 for both
statistics, say that the hotspot maps are descriptive and that inference about
project effects rests on the BAG models.

**Optional extension.** Emerging hot spot analysis
(`sfdep::emerging_hotspot_analysis`, a new dependency) on the **season-year
cubes** (22 steps), the common descriptive step. Interpret it only where the
cube is dense enough: **mobile VP** (40% of domain cell-season-years active)
and, as exploratory, mobile AFE (17%). Report the other gears as too sparse,
not as "no trend".

## Phase 4: Infrastructure data and BAG models (`02a_infrastructure.qmd`, `10_bag.qmd`) {#sec-bag}

### Ørsted turbine and cable data {#sec-infra}

**Received October 2026** and built in `02a_infrastructure.qmd` (`05` step 8
until 2026-10-28; D-060) into
`data/sf/infra/infrastructure.gpkg` (EPSG:32619), layers `foundations` and
`cables`. The source files under `data/sf/owf/*/turbines/` are read only.

| Project | Positions | Installation dates | Cable routes | Cable works window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SFW | Layout GeoJSON (2025-07-25), 13 points | Ørsted CSV (PSO id × position × day), equal to PSO report Table 3: OSS Z01 (AP06) 2023-06-19/20; 12 monopiles each on its own day(s), A12 (AP05) 2023-07-02 to A04 (AM08) 2023-08-07 | 12 inter-array + 1 export | 2023-03 to 2023-09 (PSO report) |
| RWF | Layout GeoJSON (2026-01-19), 67 points | Ørsted foundation CSV: 65 WTG 2024-05-10 to 2025-05-26 (none Sep 2024 – Apr 2025), OSS Z01a and Z02 (Oct 2024), Z01b (Aug 2025) | 65 inter-array + 3 export | Inter-array from 2025-11 (open); export complete by 2026-08 (no start) |
| SRW | Preliminary layout GeoJSON (2026-01-05), 85 points | Ørsted foundation CSV: 44 WTG 2025-06-04 to 2025-10-27; OCS-DC jacket (8 pin piles) 2025-09-06 to 09-08 | 84 inter-array + 3 export | Nearshore export by 2025-12 (no start); inter-array unknown |

**Layer schema.** `foundations`: `asset_id`, `project`, `asset_type`
(`wtg`, `oss`), `grid_pos` (e.g. AM06), `internal_id` (Ørsted's B##/C##/Z##),
`status` (`installed`, `planned`), `date_basis` (`exact`, `planned`),
`foundation_installed`, `foundation_end`, `n_date_rows`,
`wtg_installed` and `first_power` (not supplied, kept blank), `depth_m`,
`layout_offset_m`, `source`, `version_date`. `cables`: `asset_id`,
`project`, `asset_type` (`iac`, `export_cable`), `route_name`, `lay_start`,
`lay_end`, `burial_complete` (blank), `date_basis`, `source`,
`version_date`. Fields are in `references/data_dictionary.md`.

**Gaps and how they are handled** (decisions 2026-10-19, D-022 to D-026):

- **SFW turbine ids** (resolved 2026-10-20). The PSO report numbers
  monopiles A01–A15 and the layout uses grid positions; Ørsted's
  `sfw_monopile_install_orsted.csv` links the two, so each SFW foundation
  has its own installation day(s). Before it arrived, the 12 turbines shared
  the turbine window, which put seven of them (installed in July) a month
  late. The CSV's one truncated id (A01 as "AM0", on AM05) was corrected in
  the file on 2026-10-20.
- **Safety zones** (2026-10-20). Every foundation had a USCG 500 m safety
  zone from its installation through turbine and platform construction:
  SFW's were enforced 2023-05-01 to 2024-05-31; the RWF and SRW rules run to
  2027-05-31 and 2028-05-31, so their zones stay on to the end of the window.
  They become `sz_share(t)` (below; caveat 17).
- **SRW's 40 unrecorded positions** are `planned` and never count as
  installed. Work stopped in December 2025 and resumed in February 2026 with
  turbine erection on installed foundations; no public record shows further
  piling by August 2026, and the January–April piling moratorium applies. The
  sensitivity table installs them in May 2026.
- **Cable lay dates** are project-level windows, not per route. Only SFW's
  is closed; RWF's inter-array window is open to the end of the analysis
  window; the rest have no start date and never switch `cable_works` on.
- **Turbine erection and first power** were not supplied. The covariates
  therefore describe **foundations** (the seabed obstruction and the piling
  noise), and the phases end at the last known works, not at first power.

**Derived covariates per cell × month** (`05`; the month tables and
`infra_cell_month.csv`):

| Covariate | Definition |
|---|---|
| `d_found_km(t)` | Distance to the nearest foundation (WTG or substation) whose last installation day is on or before the end of month *t*; NA before the first (June 2023) |
| `n_found_2km(t)` | Installed foundations within 2 km |
| `active_construction(t)` | A foundation's installation days overlap month *t* within 5 km |
| `cable_works(t)` | A cable route whose works window overlaps month *t* lies within 2 km |
| `sz_share(t)` | Share of the cell's area inside an active USCG 500 m safety zone: each foundation's zone from its installation to its project's rule end (`references/infra_safety_zones.csv`: SFW 2024-05-31, RWF 2027-05-31, SRW 2028-05-31). Zones are unioned, so co-located foundations count once |
| `sz_share_install(t)` | The same, with each zone active only on its foundation's installation days (enforcement-only; sensitivity) |
| `phase(t)` | Nearest project's `pre` (before its first foundation or cable-lay day), `construction`, or `post_construction` (after its last works day, only if every foundation is installed and every cable window closed) |
| `months_since_first_found(t)` | Months from the nearest project's first foundation, for event-time plots |
| `d_found_final_km`, `d_cable_km` | Static: nearest eventual foundation (planned included) and nearest cable route |

The radii (2, 5, 2 km) and the SRW sensitivity month are `05` parameters.
With these data, SFW reaches `post_construction` in October 2023, while RWF
and SRW stay in `construction` to the end of the window (RWF's inter-array
works are open; SRW has unrecorded positions).

For the season-year timing model (fixed AFE), each covariate is aggregated
over the months of the season: means for distances, counts and `sz_share`,
the share of months for `active_construction` and `cable_works`, and the
phase held in most months (`infra_cell_season_year.csv` and the season-year
tables).

`05`'s gate checks the counts against the sources, that each CSV
position lies within 100 m of its layout point, that every date falls inside
the analysis window, that every foundation lies inside its own lease, and
that no cell's exposure ever decreases.

### BAG design

Before–After–Gradient (Methratta 2020, 2021) estimates the change in the
**spatial gradient** of effort with distance from the development, between
the period before and the period after. Within-AOI changes that are uniform in
space cancel out of the gradient contrast.

**Cell × stage × season × gear** (per gear, per dataset; the shared primary
BAG model, @sec-time-steps):

$$
\log \mu_{c,s,k} = \beta_0 + \beta_s + \alpha_k + f(d_c) + \gamma_s \, f(d_c) + \mathbf{z}_c^\top \boldsymbol{\delta} + \omega_c + \log(\text{months}_{s,k} \cdot \text{area}_c)
$$

- *k* ∈ {Apr–Sep, Oct–Mar} is the season. *α*<sub>k</sub> absorbs the
  seasonal level, so the stage effects are not biased by each stage's
  calendar mix (caveat 8). The offset uses the months in each stage × season
  stratum (@sec-time-steps).
- A `season × dist_band` term, letting the baseline gradient differ by
  season (for example, fixed gear working closer inshore in summer), is a
  sensitivity. It is static across stages, so it cannot stand in for the BAG
  effects *γ*<sub>s</sub>.
- *d*<sub>c</sub> is `dist_band`, with 8–15 km as the reference, or a
  low-rank smooth of `dist_lease_km`.
- **z**<sub>c</sub> holds the static environmental covariates (@sec-env):
  `s(depth_m)`, slope, BPI and, once available, habitat shares.
- *γ*<sub>s</sub> are the **BAG effects**. The change in the inside / 0–2 km
  rate ratio between Stage 1 and Stages 2 and 3 is the headline estimate.
- *ω*<sub>c</sub> is a spatial random effect (Phase 5 decides its form).

**Timing model: cell × month × gear** (VP and mobile AFE; fixed AFE at cell ×
season-year, with *s*<sub>cc</sub>(moy) replaced by the season term
*α*<sub>k</sub>). Stages are replaced by time-varying exposure:

$$
\log \mu_{c,t} = \beta_0 + s_{\text{cc}}(\text{moy}_t) + s(\text{year}_t) + h\big(d^{\text{found}}_{c}(t)\big) + \text{phase}_{p(c),t} \times g(d_c) + \lambda \, \text{active}_{c,t} + \kappa \, \text{sz}_{c,t} + \mathbf{z}_c^\top \boldsymbol{\delta} + \omega_c + \varepsilon_{c,t} + \log(\text{area}_c)
$$

- phase<sub>p,t</sub> ∈ {pre, construction, post_construction} is `phase` from
  `05`: each cell's nearest project's Ørsted dates. The three projects run on
  different schedules, which gives a **staggered design**: cells near a
  project that has not started act as concurrent controls for cells near one
  that has. With the received dates the stagger is SFW (works from March
  2023), RWF (foundations from May 2024) and SRW (foundations from June 2025),
  so every project has at least 15 months of data from its start, and RWF and SRW
  cells serve as not-yet-treated controls for 14 and 27 months after SFW
  starts. Only SFW reaches `post_construction` inside the window, so the
  operation-phase contrast rests on SFW's 76 nearest cells (count at render
  time); RWF and SRW inform the construction phase.
- **SFW has no gradient of its own.** RWF and SRW surround it, so every
  SFW-nearest cell is `inside` (62) or `0–2` km (14); none falls in the
  2–15 km bands or the 8–15 km reference. A project-specific SFW gradient
  cannot be estimated. SFW enters the timing model only through the shared
  *g*(*d*<sub>c</sub>) and *h*(·), with RWF/SRW cells as its comparison, and
  the `phase × g(d)` term should be read as an RWF + SRW gradient. (Found in
  Phase 1 step 10, 2026-10-19.)
- *h*(·) is the foundation-distance response on `d_found_km(t)`, fitted only
  after the first installation (June 2023).
- *λ* is the short-term construction effect on `active_construction(t)`
  (piling noise and vessel exclusion within 5 km), kept apart from the
  lasting presence of the structures in *h*(·). `cable_works(t)` enters the
  same way as a sensitivity, since its windows are coarse.
- *κ* is the **mandated exclusion** on `sz_share(t)`, the share of the cell
  inside an active 500 m USCG safety zone (caveat 17). With it in the
